pr_body:
As discussed in #1931 --watchfs was made a no-op on windows in d04d7baa1605c8c3a637255bd61c00dba73ad800. The reason for this is that it will hold locks for the (parent-directories of) directories it is watching. Since we recursively register the watcher this leads to locks on folders we do not want to be locked.

The issue is known and tracked at https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-6972833 but is marked as a Won't Fix. The suggested fix is to instead use ExtendedWatchEventModifier.FILE_TREE which allows a single WatchKey to recursively watch a folder on windows.

This pull request implements the FILE_TREE flag for the root folder that is being watched, and disables the registration of the recursive folders. I have tried to keep the change as small as possible, but I can imagine that we wish to separate this logic to dedicated windows class similar to the OSX variant.

Fixes #1931

Thanks for fixing `--watchfs` on Windows. I wonder if we can add a simple test for this?

Maybe replicating the MacOSXFsEventsDiffAwarenessTest is a good option. The test cases that it contains are ignored due to flakyness however. I cannot find any test scenarios for the generic WatchServiceDiffAwareness. Do you think we should introduce these or leave it untested as on other platforms?

I'm quite skeptic for introducing flakyness again due to relying on the OS to handle watching. Having used the flag for some time now I occasionally get the overflow message (I assume due to too many file changes) which bazel handles gracefully by assuming EVERYTHING_MODIFIED.
OK. Since this feature is guarded by an experimental flag, I think it's probably fine.

issue_context.title: Windows: support --watchfs
comments: Do you know what's available already?
I believe the java interface should work out of the box. So probably just wiring it and then testing it :)
Here is a link to IntelliJ IDEA's implementation: https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/master/native/fileWatcher
Java WatchService should work as intended so there is probably no change needed to the Linux one. The OSX case is tricky because the java implementation is wrong.
I'm not aware of anyone waiting for this feature, and it doesn't seem critical. (It would be nice to have, of course.)

I think it makes sense to make `--watchfs` a non-op on Windows for now. But in the long term this could be a useful feature to improve Windows performance as well, since IO operation on Windows is much slower than Mac/Linux.

I agree with @meteorcloudy .

@alexeagle , I don't think we should support disabling a flag just on one platform. I see no problem with making it a no-op on Windows though.
Cool, I will send a change for this

2019-07-08 state:
- `--watchfs` is both a (deprecated) startup flag [1] and a command flag [2]
- e73f881b66e5540051f92f8ffab5570b6856fea8 marked the startup flag deprecated on @ulfjack's request in the internal code review
- a TODO(ulfjack) [3] says the startup flag should be deleted in favor of the command flag
- d04d7baa1605c8c3a637255bd61c00dba73ad800 made the command flag a no-op on Windows, but didn't change the startup flag

I don't know if anyone wants `--watchfs` on Windows or if anyone supports it.

[1] https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/c26e3396cb341e173b4be5c780cafac3ec386df5/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/runtime/BlazeServerStartupOptions.java#L333

[2] https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/c26e3396cb341e173b4be5c780cafac3ec386df5/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/skyframe/LocalDiffAwareness.java#L51

[3] https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/c26e3396cb341e173b4be5c780cafac3ec386df5/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/runtime/BlazeOptionHandler.java#L277

I found the loading and analysing time on Windows for Angular and TensorFlow is quite long (1 ~ 2s) due to scanning every input file and directory for every bazel command. If watchfs is enabled, we can avoid many file operations, so potentially we could improve the performance a lot. I'm planning to work on this in 2019 Q3.

We are trying to migrate big codebase to Bazel and, although we support all three platforms, primary Dev machines are Windows. Typical Dev workflow includes frequent incremental rebuilds after making very small changes. Attempt to take big external dependencies (think Boost and Qt) as sources makes this even more important. We expect that working --watchfs on Windows would improve Dev experience dramatically.

@meteorcloudy were you able to start working on this feature? Any bits we can try? We are waiting for this feature desperately.
@konste I'm sorry, --watchfs for Windows is no longer a priority currently. I don't have plan to work on this, but contribution is always welcome!
